title: kamado.config.jsonc
description: Configuration of kamado v3. Relative paths are resolved against the directory of this file. Unknown options are errors.

globs.description: A glob or a list of globs. Negated globs ("!...") are not supported; use the matching ignore/exclude option.

label.description: A text, or a text per language of the screen of kamado ui (the keys are languages such as "en" and "ja"; a language the screen does not speak is never shown). The text is looked for in the language of the screen, then in "en". null and an empty text are the same as not writing it.

banner.description: A comment put at the top of each output. Placeholders: {{date:FORMAT}}, {{year}}, {{version}}. An empty string or false turns it off.

sourcemap.description: true writes it always, false never, "onServer" (default) only for the dev server.

format.description: false leaves the markup as it is. An object sets the printing options.

minify.description: false turns every minification off. An object picks them.

serializer.description: How the markup is written: "linkedom" (as v2 did) or "spec" (as the HTML standard says: & and no-break space escaped in attribute values,   in text, class="" kept, <path></path>).

encoding.description: The character encoding the pages are written in: UTF-8, or Shift_JIS (Windows, CP932). A page can name its own in html.overrides.

entities.description: "none", "all", or a map from a character to its reference.

overrides.description: Options for the pages that match "pages".

site.description: Falls back to production.* of package.json.

overrides.description: Path of a JSON file with virtual pages and metadata overrides.

sitemap.description: false does not write a sitemap.

host.description: The address the server listens on ("0.0.0.0" for every interface). Requests may name it too; other names that reach the machine go in allowedHosts.

allowedHosts.description: Host names the dev server answers besides localhost, IP literals and host (ASCII; an internationalized name in punycode). ".example.test" matches example.test and every subdomain of it. An IP address here admits the pages on that address (a tool on another machine) as origins of cross-site requests.

proxy.description: Keyed by path prefix (starts with "/"). The value is a target URL or a rule object.

report.description: Path of the JSON file the build result is written to.

ui.description: What kamado ui shows, shared with the team through the repository. Only kamado ui reads it: the build and the dev server do not.

keys.description: Metadata key -> how the table presents it. The label is the heading of the column; the key and the description are shown on hover and in the column menu. Without a label the key itself is the heading. It applies to the columns of metadata keys, not to the fixed columns (url, inputPath ...), and a key that no page has gets no column.

syncFunctions.description: The operations of the sync button of kamado ui, and of kamado sync. Each runs a script of the project: an import (`read`) changes the files of the local repository to the pages the outside data has, and an export (`write`) changes the outside data to the pages of the repository. kamado finds the difference and asks for a confirmation before anything is applied or written. Only a sync reads and runs them: the build, the dev server and kamado ui itself do not run a script.

name.description: What `kamado sync <name>` and the screen call the operation by. Not empty, and different for each operation; any character is allowed (the command looks at the names before it takes its argument for a path).

label.description: The name of the operation on the screen: a text, or a text per language (the keys are languages such as "en" and "ja"). Looked for in the language of the screen, then in "en", then the name is shown. Required, and not null.

script.description: The ES module of the script, relative to the directory of this file. Its default export is an object `{ select?, read?, write? }`, which Node imports as it is: with `write` it is an export, without it an import (`read` is needed).
